exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Ether (ETH) traded at $1,635.01 as of 2026-11-21 10:07:58 UTC, +0.67% over one hour and -6.63% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $1,542.97 to $1,756.42; spot sits at 43% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is -13.54% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($1,642.38) is below the 72-hour average ($1,729.09). Spot is 14.50% below the seven-day high of $1,912.26 and 5.97% above the seven-day low of $1,542.97.

exhibits.title: Volatility & Momentum
exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 4.87% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 57.2, conventionally neutral.

exhibits.title: Liquidity
exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $26.19 billion, equal to 13.11% of the $199.84 billion market capitalization.

exhibits.title: Market Sentiment
exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 12 ("Extreme Fear"), versus 13 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink ETH/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $1,637.57, 39 minutes before the spot quote and +0.16% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price of ETH is firmly entrenched at $1,635.01, a 0.67% gain in the last hour, indicating short‑term buying pressure despite a 6.63% dip over 24 hours, and the price sits in the lower‑mid segment of its 24‑hour range, positioning it for a rebound toward the $1,756 high [Ex. A, B].  

2. Volume remains robust at $26.19 billion, representing 13.11% of market cap, while fear is extreme (CFGI 12), a classic contrarian signal that buyers are poised to re‑enter as risk appetite improves [Ex. E, F].  

3. The Chainlink oracle, the official settlement reference, posted $1,637.57, only 0.16% above the spot, confirming that any practice entry will be executed at a level essentially identical to the market, eliminating slippage risk [Ex. G].  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The market is in a pronounced downtrend: ETH has lost 13.54% over seven days and is 14.50% below its recent high, indicating continued selling pressure that will likely keep price below the current spot of $1,635.01 [Ex. C].  

2. Liquidity remains robust while sentiment is at an “Extreme Fear” level, a classic contrarian bullish signal; with $26.19 billion traded in 24 h, any modest buying influx can quickly lift price toward the mid‑range of the 24‑hour band where the spot sits at only 43% of that range [Ex. B, E, F].  

3. Realized volatility is modest (4.87% per day) and RSI is neutral at 57.2, suggesting the market is not over‑extended and is poised for a short‑term rebound; the Chainlink feed, our settlement reference, is only 0.16% above spot, confirming a stable pricing foundation [Ex. D, G].  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s “pronounced downtrend” claim ignores the immediate price momentum: over the past hour ETH rose 0.67% while the 24‑hour RSI of 57.2 is already in neutral‑to‑bull territory, indicating short‑term buying strength that can overcome the seven‑day decline [Ex. A, D]. Second, the Bear’s “Extreme Fear” bullish contrarian argument is overstated; the Fear & Greed Index is at 12, but the market’s realized volatility remains modest at 4.87% per day, suggesting limited speculative influx and that price will likely remain confined near the lower‑mid of the 24‑hour range rather than surge toward the midpoint [Ex. D, F, B]. Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s “short‑term buying pressure” claim rests on a solitary 0.67% hourly uptick, yet the seven‑day trend is a 13.54% decline and the 24‑hour average ($1,642.38) remains below the 72‑hour average ($1,729.09), demonstrating sustained bearish momentum [Ex. C]. Moreover, the “lower‑mid segment” argument ignores that the price sits at only 43% of its 24‑hour range, far nearer the bottom than the top, leaving little room for a rebound to $1,756 [Ex. B]. The “extreme fear” contrarian signal is muted by a neutral RSI of 57.2 and a realized volatility of 4.87% per day, indicating no decisive oversold condition [Ex. D]. Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds the evidence insufficient to justify a practice position.

findings.finding: Price rose 0.67% in the last hour but is down 6.63% over 24 h, showing mixed short‑term momentum.
Current price sits at 43% of the 24‑hour range, nearer the lower bound, limiting upside potential.
Seven‑day decline of 13.54% and price below both 24‑h and 72‑h averages indicate a prevailing downtrend.
Fear & Greed Index at 12 signals extreme fear, a contrarian bullish cue but not decisive alone.
Realized volatility 4.87% per day and RSI 57.2 are modest and neutral, offering no clear directional bias.

ruling.opinion: The Court notes that while the hour‑to‑hour rise and extreme‑fear sentiment suggest a possible short‑term lift, the broader seven‑day downtrend, low position within the daily range, and neutral technical indicators collectively temper bullish expectations. No single side presents a dominant case, leading to dismissal of a practice position.
ruling.dissent: The Bear argues that the sustained seven‑day decline and low placement in the daily range outweigh any contrarian fear signal, warranting a short stance.

sentence.reason: The case was dismissed; no practice position is ordered.
